lesson.title: Continuing the Alphabet: ਟ, ਠ, ਡ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned ਛ, ਜ, and ਝ. Today, three more letters that use a new tongue movement: ਟ, ਠ, and ਡ!

ਟ, ਠ, and ਡ are made by curling the tip of your tongue back and touching the roof of your mouth — a genuinely different feeling from the letters you've learned so far. Practice saying all three together: ta (tongue curled)... tha (curled, breathier)... da (curled). Notice how different this feels from a regular 't' or 'd' sound.
You now know a new row of letters that use this tongue-curl sound! Tomorrow we'll finish this row and start learning colors.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਟ, ਠ, and ਡ
Physically notice the tongue-curling articulation distinguishing this row
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review ਛ, ਜ, ਝ from last week.
2. Introduce ਟ, ਠ, ਡ, having the child physically feel their tongue curl back for each.
3. Practice all three sounds together.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more.
5. Close by counting all the letters learned across both weeks so far.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just ਟ and ਡ (the clearest contrast) before adding ਠ's breathier version
Ready for more: ask the child to compare this new tongue-curl sound to a similar-sounding letter they already know
This is a genuinely new articulation point — worth real repetition before moving faster
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਟ, ਠ, ਡ continue the Painti Akhari sequence from last week's ਛ/ਜ/ਝ, introducing the retroflex consonant row. Every letter was validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing.

worksheet.title: Continuing the Alphabet: ਟ, ਠ, ਡ

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its sound out loud, then write it once more on your own.
